rewrite.stem: A 52-year-old man presents to his primary care physician with a 2-week history of palpitations and mild fatigue. He denies chest pain, shortness of breath, or syncope. He has no significant past medical history and takes no medications. His pulse is 88/min and irregular; blood pressure is 128/74 mmHg. An ECG shows an irregularly irregular ventricular rate with no discernible P waves. A bedside transthoracic echocardiogram reveals normal left ventricular function and no valvular abnormalities. Which of the following is the most appropriate initial diagnostic test?
rewrite.lead_in: Which of the following is the most appropriate initial diagnostic test?
rewrite.explanation: This patient has new-onset atrial fibrillation (AF) without an obvious precipitant—he is relatively young, has no structural heart disease on echocardiogram, and no known cardiovascular risk factors. In all patients with new-onset AF, serum TSH should be measured to rule out hyperthyroidism, as it is a reversible trigger that can present as AF as its sole manifestation. Cardiac catheterization (A) is not indicated without evidence of myocardial ischemia. Exercise stress testing (B) is used to evaluate for CAD, but is low-yield in an otherwise healthy patient. Holter monitoring (C) isL- yield in this case because AF has already been documented on the ECG, making further rhythm capture redundant. Transesophageal echocardiography (E) is used to exclude left atrial thrombus before cardioversion, which is a subsequent management step, not the first diagnostic priority.
rewrite.teaching_point: Serum TSH must be checked in all patients with new-onset AF because hyperthyroidism is a reversible trigger that can present with AF as its only manifestation.

distractor_rationale.A: No anginal symptoms or risk factors to warrant invasive coronary evaluation
distractor_rationale.B: CAD-related AF is unlikely in a young, otherwise healthy patient; stress test is not the initial step in AF workup
distractor_rationale.C: AF is already documented on the 12-lead ECG; additional ambulatory monitoring does not change the immediate workup priority
distractor_rationale.E: TEE is used pre-cardioversion to exclude left atrial appendage thrombus—appropriate later, not as the initial test
